summary.headline: Automotive Axles Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 18% QoQ to INR6,643 million, with PAT margin steady at 8%; FY26 revenue INR21,777 million (+5%).
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR6,643 million, up about 18% QoQ and 18.5-18.7% YoY, with EBITDA of INR825 million (12.4%) and PAT of INR539 million (8%), matching Q4 FY25's PAT margin. FY26 revenue grew 5% to INR21,777 million, with EBITDA of INR2,692 million (12.4%) before a one-time workmen settlement of about INR120 million, which takes reported EBITDA to 10.6% (10.1% in FY25). Management said the industry's 7.5T+ CV market closed FY26 at about 480,000 units (+16%), and that the company operates at 70-80% of capacity in soft months after about 90% in Q4. Management said Phase 1 and 1A capacity will be complete by end-December 2026, with a next capex phase to be defined over the next 6-12 months.

financial_highlights.value: ~68% of revenue (INR4,518 million per transcript; figure as stated)

financial_highlights.change: Flat QoQ; includes one-offs such as leave encashment (~8% of quarter cost)
Similar to Q4 FY25 PAT margin of ~8%

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 total income incl. other income

financial_highlights.value: INR2,692 million (12.4%); 10.6% after ~INR120 million exceptional (annualised workmen settlement)
About INR70-73 crore (per analyst's figure); management stated ~INR30 crore spent in FY26 with net cash generation of INR30 crore after investments
financial_highlights.change: Remaining committed capex 60-70% spent in FY25

segments.name: Heavy-duty axles (core)
segments.commentary: Management says the core is heavy-duty (50T+ tonnage) axles, with the 185 single axle, tandem and HR axles covering 70-80 tonne ranges. The 4x2 tractor-trailer product launched about 2-3 years ago is being ramped up across major customers.

segments.name: LCV/ICV
segments.commentary: Less than 5% of revenue, per management. Company says it will not extend beyond certain GBW/GAW levels, with focus staying on heavier vehicles. Slipper suspension supply continues to the largest customer under a supply-chain handover agreement.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the domestic CV market to stay at 400,000+ units in FY27 (FY26 was ~480,000); analysts were told the range could be 420-450k-480k, and it is too early to call.
Long-term top line is targeted at roughly INR4,000-5,000 crore, with exports a larger share than today; management cited this as the direction over the next several years.
Capex in FY27 is expected to be similar in size to FY26 (~INR70 crore per Raman K.'s statement; a figure of INR30 crore was spent in FY26), with the next phase to be defined in 6-12 months.
Management declined to give forward margin guidance but said efficiency gains should offset inflation and product mix effects, with fixed-cost absorption improving as top line grows.
Technical fee payable to Meritor HVS is 4-4.5% of revenue, depending on the domestic/export mix, and is accrued monthly; all reported quarterly results are stated after this fee.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 and 1A capacity expected to be completed by end-December 2026, per management.
Management said current utilisation was about 90% in Q4 FY26 and is typically 70-80% in soft months such as April-May 2026.
Capacity: management said there are no capacity constraints unless the market runs above Q4 FY26 volumes.
A further capex phase (the 'next set of investment') to be decided within 6-12 months, based on domestic and export outlook; amount not disclosed.
Management said the capex will also bring in new technology and efficient equipment to offset fixed-cost inflation.
demand_pricing: Industry: FY26 CV (7.5T+) market at ~480,000 units, +16% YoY; FY23 +37%, and variation within 5% from FY23 to FY25 per Kishan Kumar Udupi.
Q1-Q2 FY27 expected to be a typically soft period; the company is seeing consistent demand, and management said diesel price impacts are too early to assess.

Tractor-trailer (4x2) share rising; rigid multi-axle proportion falling. Management said this cannibalises some rigid products but not business, and the total tonnage of the industry reached 9.4 million tonnes in FY26 versus 8.7 million in FY19.
Commodity pass-through: back-to-back arrangements with most customers; financials are trued up for recent steel increases, with recovery timing that can lag.
New-product realisation uplift vs legacy: management said 10-25% for tandem vs single axle, not 2-3x; new products carry marginally better profitability.
Export: volumes limited to assemblies, subassemblies and child parts in Europe and North America, because product configurations differ and customisation is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much technical fee does the company pay Meritor HVS under the new sales agreement?
qa_highlights.answer: Raman K. said the technical fee is 4-4.5% of revenue, depending on the revenue mix; it is accrued monthly and included in all reported quarterly results.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook and can exports drive the INR4,500-5,000 crore top line target?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishan Kumar Udupi said the top line could reach about INR4,000-5,000 crore, with exports a larger share, but export scope is limited to subassemblies and child parts in Europe and North America.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and when does new capacity come online?
qa_highlights.answer: Nagaraja Gargeshwari said Q4 was about 90% and April-May softened to 70-80%; Phase 1 and 1A are to be completed by end-December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How does the rise in tractor-trailer demand affect axle volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishan said the shift to 4x2 tractor-trailers reduces rigid multi-axle units but the company has the product and does not expect business loss; the industry TIV is expected to exceed 500,000 by FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Will the capex in FY27 be similar to FY26, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Raman K. said FY27 capex will be broadly similar to the ~INR70 crore of the year; Nagaraja declined to give margin guidance but said efficiency gains should protect margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook in light of diesel price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Nagaraja said demand is stable and the industry is expected to stay at 400,000+ in FY27; diesel impact is too early to comment.

risks_watch: The new technical fee (4-4.5% of revenue) to Meritor HVS flows through reported margins; watch the disclosed net margin after the fee going forward.
Tractor-trailer shift could cannibalise rigid multi-axle volumes; watch the mix of new 4x2 product versus legacy products.
Q1-Q2 FY27 is seasonally soft; utilisation fell from ~90% to 70-80% in April-May 2026.
Steel and commodity price increases are pass-through with lag; watch working capital and margin timing.
The next capex phase has no amount or timeline beyond 6-12 months; the company has not yet disclosed the investment size.
Interim CFO in place; a permanent CFO appointment is not mentioned in the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and execution, with management describing FY26 as a high-note close and Q4 as a record for the industry. Evasive on forward numbers: margin guidance, the size of the next capex phase, Meritor fee disclosure beyond the 4-4.5% range, and export-specific revenue were deferred or not quantified.

growth.why: No explicit FY27 revenue growth guidance; management expects domestic CV market at 400k+ units in FY27 versus ~480k in FY26 (a decline), with Phase 1/1A capacity due by end-December 2026 and FY27 capex similar to FY26 (~INR70 crore), and no forward margin guidance.
